items.title: Strata 0.2.11: support for Unsloth Dynamic v3.1 Qwen3.8-Flash-Next quants and layer splitting for every configuration
items.summary: The Strata local inference app shipped v0.2.11. It adds support for Unsloth's new Dynamic v3.1 Qwen3.8-Flash-Next GGUF quants (seven 1 to 4 bit variants, for example UD-IQ1_M at 68 GB), allows layer splitting in all configurations, and brings speed and app/terminal improvements. Daniel Han of Unsloth confirmed the UDv3.1 quants run in Strata, including UDv3.1 DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash GGUFs.

reception.summary: Users report faster decode after upgrading (one quote reports 70 to 110 tok/s at 256K context on their setup; a reply cites 31 to 62.7 tok/s on a single 12 GB card). Open questions are about AMD Radeon support and Windows RAM use. No Community Note; a small off-topic political spat in replies.

items.title: ServerBench (CMU): coding agents build a full LLM serving stack; Claude Sonnet 5.5's Gemma E4B system gives 4.87x the value per GPU dollar of the vLLM reference
items.summary: A CMU benchmark asks coding agents to design a complete, specialized serving system and pick its concurrency. The score is latency-qualified token value per dollar of GPU cost, measured by replaying real coding sessions, with an independent check that the system works. Across 11 coding-agent models and three deployments, 22 of 33 runs produced a verified system and 13 beat the strongest baseline. The best run (Claude Sonnet 5.5, Gemma E4B) reached 4.87x the vLLM reference. Failed runs often shipped untested code paths.

items.title: AutoSFT: a multi-agent framework that automates SFT data research, lifting IFEval by 6.5 points at the same budget
items.summary: THUNLP, BUPT, ModelBest, UIUC and CUHK split SFT data research into roles: an executor, four analysis subagents (training data, failure cases, learning dynamics, research history), a synthesis writer with a verifier, and a meta agent that picks the next recipe. A single-agent baseline only tuned mixture ratios over 33 rounds. AutoSFT used all six data-action families, hit IFEval 63.33 by round 6 (above the baseline's best over 50 rounds) and 67.10 by round 30. Synthesis alone added IFEval +3.4, IFBench +2.9 and MBPP+ +3.7. Paper and code are public.

items.title: Gradium's on-device Phonon TTS takes first place on intelligibility in German and Spanish on the Open TTS Leaderboard
items.summary: Hugging Face's Lysandre Debut highlights Gradium's Phonon results on the Open TTS Leaderboard: first place on intelligibility (WER/CER) in German and Spanish, top three in every language it was evaluated on, and the lead in CPU streaming time-to-first-audio, against models up to 100x its size. He notes the leaderboard scores intelligibility, throughput and latency, predicted naturalness and voice-clone similarity separately, so these wins are specific rather than an overall best.

doubt.pushback: Results are as reported by Gradium; the post itself says per-dimension wins do not make it best across use cases.

items.title: NVIDIA paper: interactive world simulation with Cosmos 3, with open code and four Cosmos3-Nano-Sim checkpoints
items.summary: NVIDIA adapts Cosmos 3 world foundation models for real-time, action-driven world simulation: streaming observations in response to actions and scene controls, using temporal-causal attention, causal distillation and self-forcing, and streaming inference. The paper shows camera navigation, bimanual robot manipulation, controllable video transfer and multi-view autonomous-vehicle simulation with LiDAR. It releases code (Cosmos, Cosmos-Framework) and open-weight checkpoints Cosmos3-Nano-Sim-Bimanual, -Sim-Transfer, -Sim-Auto and -Transfer-Auto.
